title: Profile the Invoice Inbox
scenario: It is 8:00 AM at Beacon Manufacturing's accounts-payable desk. Before you build anything, understand the raw material. Three invoices have landed overnight - read the inbox like an automation designer: who sends these, what shape do they arrive in, what would a system need to ingest them, and who reads them next?
input: 3 documents in the AP shared mailbox. (1) INV-58831 from Northwind Fasteners - a PDF attachment, 500 M8 hex bolts against PO-7742, total $1,220.00. (2) INV-58832 from Cascade Packaging - an emailed image of a paper invoice. (3) INV-58833 from Northwind Fasteners - a portal export (CSV). Same mailbox, three different formats, arriving on no fixed schedule. We follow INV-58831 through the whole desk today.
instructions: Read the inbox as a source, not as data to extract - extraction is the Invoice Record task.
Answer the four source questions against the inbox and the workflow map.
Validate to mint the source profile.

questions.prompt: Who produces the documents in this inbox?

options.text: The AP Clerk, by typing them each morning
Vendors, who send invoices to Beacon's shared mailbox and portal

questions.explain: Invoices originate outside Beacon - vendors like Northwind Fasteners send them. The AP Clerk receives and processes them; it does not author them.

questions.prompt: What shape do these invoices arrive in?

options.text: One consistent structured feed with named fields
A single CSV table the mailbox produces
Mixed formats - PDF, emailed image, portal CSV - on no fixed schedule

questions.explain: Look at the inbox: a PDF, a photographed paper invoice, and a portal export all landed in the same mailbox. Format variety and irregular timing are exactly what makes intake hard.

questions.prompt: In a real company, what would ingesting this inbox require?

options.text: Shared mailbox access, portal credentials, and document storage permission
The Controller to read each email first

questions.explain: The documents live in a shared mailbox and a vendor portal, and every original must be retained for audit. Reading them programmatically means access to those channels plus a retention policy. The lab simulates this with local document fixtures.

questions.prompt: Which workflow step consumes these invoices first?
questions.explain: Follow the map's edge from this node: the inbox's first stop is the Invoice Record task that extracts each document into a structured record.

successMessage: Source profiled. You now know where every payment starts - next, you will turn one invoice into a structured record.

intro.heading: Before you build: the inbox is the source

sections.title: Why inspect before building
sections.body: Payables automation fails at the inputs more often than at the logic. Before extracting anything, a designer profiles the source: who sends it, on what schedule, in what shape, behind what access.

sections.title: A pile of documents is still a feed
sections.body: These invoices are unstructured and inconsistent, but they still arrive every day from the same vendors into the same mailbox. Recognizing that recurring pile as a feed is what makes it automatable at all.

sections.title: Lab vs work
sections.body: In the lab the inbox is a set of local document fixtures. At work it is a shared mailbox and a vendor portal - and ingesting it needs access, credentials, and an audit retention policy. The workflow map records both realities.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: Passing the inspection mints a source profile - a small record proving this input is understood. Profiling inputs is itself a real deliverable in automation work.

takeaway.heading: Source profiled
points: You answered the four source questions: producer, format, access, first consumer.
The inbox is a recurring feed of mixed-format documents - which is exactly why the next step (Invoice Record) must exist to structure them.
The lab honestly simulates the access problem: local document fixtures stand in for mailbox and portal permissions plus audit retention.
Your source profile is stored - profiling inputs is the first deliverable of any real payables automation project.
The workflow can now identify where every invoice enters the payables desk.
